welcome.heading: Welcome
welcome.intro: Tools for figuring out the best way to spend your Banknotes in Last Asylum: Plague, computed live from manually harvested pack data. Every value is based on the game's own deal percentages, your weekly Banknote spend and how much each item matters to you.
welcome.rankingsDescription: Every package and pass ranked by how much value it brings for its price. A ratio of 1.0 or more = worth buying at your weekly spend.
welcome.calendarDescription: What runs when: the event schedule with a forecast for the coming weeks, and the packs on sale on fixed weekdays.
welcome.eventsDescription: Pick an event: which of its packs to buy at your weekly spend, what to buy with its coins (in unlock order) and whether spending more on it still pays off.
welcome.sourcesDescription: Pick an item and see every pack and shop offer that gives it, even nested in chests and supplies, ranked by what one unit costs.
welcome.choicesDescription: Pick a choice chest, a package with options, or a group you can only buy one of (e.g. calendar packs) and see which is worth the most.
welcome.spendRewardsDescription: Pick a cumulative spend-reward track and see up to which tier spending more still pays off.
welcome.gearDescription: A squad's UR gear: in which order to craft it and to raise its levels and stars, step by step.
welcome.itemsDescription: Tell the tool which items you don't care about and which are extra important to you. Every page uses it.
welcome.compareDescription: Pick two items with amounts: what each is worth, and the cheapest way to get it.

settings.heading: Settings
settings.countVipPoints: Count VIP points in the worth
settings.impact: Affects every value on every page
settings.vipOn: On: values follow the game's deal %, where VIP points are part of a pack's price.
settings.vipOff: Off (default): VIP points are worth nothing; each pack's other contents carry its price (coins, pickaxes and what they buy rise).

quality.heading: Model quality
quality.medianInfo: How far off a typical pack is from its deal % (0 % = exact). Higher with VIP points off, since the game's deal % counts them.
quality.withinInfo: How many packs the fitted worths reproduce to within {limit} of what their deal % says.
quality.holdOutInfo: The honest figure: the fit has {parameters} values for {packages} packs, so it matches them closely. Here the fit is redone without each pack in turn and measures how far off that pack then is, with nothing of it seen. The typical pack is this far off; the higher it is above the first figure, the less the worths can be trusted.
quality.uncertainInfo: Items the packs hardly pin down (they appear in few packs, or only alongside the same items). Their worths are the least reliable; the Items page marks them as uncertain.

how.otherPickMeaning: Only one of a group can be bought (one Calendar Gift per month); the plan buys another.
how.monthly: Calendar Gifts and the Premium Monthly Pass count at their weekly share of the price (7/30, 7/14); the info icon at the price shows it.
how.hidden: Packs of events you haven't selected are hidden. Entries with items of unknown worth sit below the ranking, unranked.
how.coins: What to buy with event coins and diamonds is on the Shopping Plan page.

events.heading: Shopping Plan
events.description: Pick a selected event (or the VIP Shop) to see its part of the best plan for your weekly spend: the event packs to buy, the coins they give, which shop offers to buy with them (in unlock order) and whether spending more on the event still pays off.
events.details: It's the same plan as on the Pack Ranking page, so both pages agree.
events.tickHint: Only events selected under "Events this week" are listed.
events.selectPrompt: Select an event or shop above.
events.summaryNoPacks: Your plan buys none of this event's packs at your weekly spend.
events.bonusSection: Bonus tiers: extra rewards once enough has been spent in the shop
events.mineNote: Each pickaxe digs one tile; finding the floor's wish reward clears it. Unused pickaxes carry over to the next run, the floors don't: the plan only digs a run that reaches the last progress reward, and never past it (the floors above are listed for comparison). Pickaxes = per stretch of floors at the safety you chose above (up to the last progress reward; above it the average), cost = what they cost in the packs on sale (after your owned and free pickaxes), floor by floor from the bottom (the cheapest pack per pickaxe first, within its limits for the days left, whole pack prices), worth = one wish reward per floor (the best one for you), the other tiles' rewards found on the way and the progress reward for clearing the last floor (Details lists every reward).

events.mineStopPast: You've reached floor {target}: the floors above give no progress reward. Save your pickaxes for the next run: they carry over, the floors don't.
events.mineSaveText: Buying the rest isn't worth it at your weekly spend. Keep your pickaxes for the next run: they carry over, the floors don't.
events.mineSaveBudget: The rest would cost more than your weekly spend of {budget}. Keep your pickaxes for the next run: they carry over, the floors don't.
events.mineSaveUnreachable: The event's packs can't give enough in the days left to reach floor {target}. Keep your pickaxes for the next run: they carry over, the floors don't.

mineSafety.title: How sure do you want to be? The digs are random, so floor {target} takes more or fewer pickaxes from floor {from}. The plan counts with your choice:
mineSafety.average: average: enough in about 1 of 2 runs
mineSafety.max: always enough (worst case: every floor only at its pity)

mineDetails.loot: The other tiles found on the way (expected)

mineRules.tiles: Every floor has {tiles} tiles: the wish reward you picked and {normals} normal tiles. Each dig costs 1 {pickaxe} and uncovers one hidden tile; finding the wish clears the floor.
mineRules.weights: Which tile a dig uncovers is random by weight: every normal tile {normal}, the wish {wish} (it gets likelier the more you dig on a floor).
mineRules.pity: Pity: after this many digs on a floor the next one surely finds the wish, by the floor number's last digit.
mineRules.normal: Normal tiles (the same on every floor):
mineRules.free: {pickaxe} for free: {perDay} a day, {bonus} more on days you buy a pack.
mineRules.carry: Up to {floors} floors per run, but only floors up to {target} have progress rewards. {pickaxe}: what you don't use carries over to the next run; the floors start again at 1.

sources.heading: Item Sources
sources.description: Pick an item to see every pack and shop offer on sale this week that gives it, including packs where it only comes nested (e.g. SR Resource Supplies → Herbs).
sources.details: Pick-one chests count as picking this item, random chests at their expected amount (~), generic items where they can be used. Per unit = Banknotes per unit, shown per 1,000 or 1,000,000 units for bulk items (shop offers at what their coins cost: bought from the cheapest packs on sale that give them, each as often as it can be bought per week, the whole pack price counted for the coins; coins no pack sells at what they are worth in your plan). Ratio = the whole source's worth ÷ price, as on the Pack Ranking (1.0 or more = a good deal at your weekly spend). Item share = how much of that worth is this item. Item ratio = worth of just this item ÷ price (≈ ratio × item share). Sources are ranked by item ratio, which is the same as cheapest per unit first. Rows highlighted green are in the best plan for your weekly spend.

spendRewards.heading: Spend Rewards
spendRewards.description: Pick a cumulative spend-reward track to see whether pushing past your weekly spend for its next tiers pays off.
spendRewards.details: Tiers your weekly spend already reaches are marked. For each further tier: the extra Banknotes on top of your weekly spend (or the previous tier), what those Banknotes buy (the best packs still available) and the tier's reward. Step ratio 1.0 or more = the step is at least as good as your last Banknote at your weekly spend.

gear.heading: Gear Upgrade Path
gear.description: The order to craft and upgrade a squad's UR gear (sword, armor, gauntlets, boots), one squad at a time.

help.aboutText: It tells you which gear upgrade to do next for your squad. Do the step in the game, tick it off here, and the page shows you the next one.
help.squadText: Choose your hero faction with the coloured buttons at the top. All three factions follow the same steps, only the heroes are different. Each faction keeps its own progress.
help.formationText: The squad stands in two rows: two tanks in front, the carries and the support behind them.
help.boardText: Next to each hero are its four gear pieces, always in the same place:
help.tileText: Each piece shows its level and its stars. A faded piece isn’t crafted yet.
help.nextText: A dashed frame shows what the next step will change, in the colour of its list:
help.craftText: First, every hero gets all four pieces: {count} pieces, one after the other. Craft the piece in the game, then click {done}.
help.craftAllText: Already crafted everything? {craftAll} ticks them all off at once.
help.craftUnlock: The upgrades unlock as soon as everything is crafted.
help.upgradesText: Now there are two cards, one above the other: the next level step and the next star step. Do either one. Each list keeps its own order.
help.levelText: Raise a piece’s level, up to Lv {max}. No blueprints needed.
help.starsText: Add stars to a piece. Uses {ur} for the first 4 stars and {mr} for the 5th.
help.blockedTitle: Why a step can be blocked
help.blockedIntro: Levels and stars need each other: a higher level needs more stars, and more stars need a higher level.
help.blockedText: When a step needs more stars or a higher level first, its card shows {blocked} under the buttons and says what it needs. Go on with the other list until then. For example:
help.holdText: Tick the switch on the star card. The steps to 5 ★ wait, everything else goes on. Untick it once you have {item}.
help.undoText: {undo} takes back the last step of that list. It’s greyed out while a later step depends on it, and crafting can’t be undone once you’ve started upgrading.
help.listText: Open the full list under the cards and click a step to jump there: everything before it counts as done, everything after it as not done.
help.resetText: {startOver} clears the progress of the faction shown.
help.savedText: Your progress is saved in this browser only, for each faction separately.

allDone.craft: Every hero has all their UR gear.

gear.blockedByStars: Lv {level} needs {stars} ★ first ({below} ★ only allow up to Lv {cap}).
gear.neverStars: Lv {level} needs {stars} ★, but no star step gets there. The guide needs fixing.
gear.neverLevel: {target} needs Lv {level}, but no level step gets there. The guide needs fixing.
gear.locked: Unlocks once all {count} pieces are crafted.
gear.choiceHint: Have Gear Blueprints? Take the star step. Otherwise the level step.
gear.holdMr: No {item} yet: put the 5 ★ steps on hold
gear.onlyHeldLeft: Only the {count} steps to 5 ★ are left. They wait for your Gear Blueprint (MR).
gear.heldNote: {count} steps to 5 ★ are on hold until you have

valuation.summary: At a weekly spend of {budget} Banknotes, your last Banknote buys {rate} points, so worth = points ÷ {rate}.
valuation.summaryUnbound: Everything worth buying this week costs only {spent} of your {budget} Banknotes; the weakest pack bought returns {rate} points per Banknote, so worth = points ÷ {rate}.
valuation.followOn: On: the events and passes running today (green dot) are selected, and kept up to date on every page. Selecting or unselecting one yourself turns this off.
valuation.followOff: Off: your own selection. Turn on to select what the calendar shows running today and keep following it.

items.heading: Item Priorities
items.description: How much each item matters to you.
items.details: "Don't care" counts it as worthless, "Low" at half, "High" at 1.5 times its usual worth. Only base items are listed: chests, supplies, choice chests and omni shards follow the items they contain (e.g. Antitoxin Level Supplies follow Antitoxin). A crafting chain is listed once, under its top item: Tempered Steel also sets Refined Iron, Brass, Leather and Cloth. Everything follows automatically, on every page.
items.exportHint: Download your item priorities as a file, to share them with others.
items.importHint: Load item priorities from someone's file. They replace yours.
items.importedSkipped: Imported {count} item priorities; {skipped} unknown items were skipped.
items.importFailed: This file doesn't contain item priorities.
items.footnote: Worth = Banknotes per unit at the weekly spend set on the Pack Ranking page. Uncertain = the game's deal % values barely determine the item (hover the info icon for why).
items.uncertainTitle: The packs barely determine this value (e.g. it only appears in one pack next to other unknown items).
items.explainUnknown: Unknown = there's nothing to base a worth on: the item isn't in any pack with a deal %, can't be derived from other items and has no recipe (or it's deliberately not modelled, like Moon Coins). It counts as 0 inside packs.
items.explainUncertain: A number with "uncertain" is the best estimate, but it rests on thin evidence: the packs barely tell it apart from other items, or it depends on a single pack. Hover the info icon for the reason. If it looks off to you, use Low or High to correct it.
items.derivedNote: made of other items; set those instead and reset this one to Normal

compare.heading: Compare
compare.details: You see what each is worth at your weekly spend, and the cheapest guaranteed way to get it within the chosen days (from today; weekly limits reset on Monday), including what else you get along the way.
compare.note: Random chests only count with what they guarantee.
